acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: We meet the doctors. Rana Awdish spends hours of each day walking the floors of the ICU checking in on her co-workers, which means that maybe more than any single person in the hospital she knows best what the staff has been going through at each stage of this pandemic. One doctor that has deep ties to Detroit is Geneva Tatem. She’s one of the few Black doctors in the ICU and has a deep awareness of what Covid-19 has done to families in the city.
acts.credits: By Miki Meek, Robyn Semien, Ira Glass

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: When it comes to caring for Covid-19 patients, it’s the nurses who are carrying the heaviest burden. Ben Calhoun spent weeks talking to the nurses in the first Covid-19 unit to open in the ICU – Pod 4.
acts.title: Pod Bless America

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: We found out about a patient from a recording made by young doctor named Stan Linder. Producer Emanuele Berry put this together. It begins with a voice memo Stan recorded for us on his phone.
acts.title: Stan’s Good Day

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Robert Granger was a patient in Pod 4 for several weeks. During that time, his daughter learns something about him she'd never realized before.
acts.title: Granger in a Strange Land

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Some of the first Covid-19 patients to arrive at Henry Ford Hospital were police and others who’d attended a community breakfast in early March called "Police and Pancakes." Aaron K. Foley has this story of this breakfast and of one man — Marlowe Stoudamire — who ended up at Henry Ford.
acts.title: Mr. Eastside
